Thank you for your interest in the Public Panel on Libraries. This Panel is part of The Great Library Debate. 

The Panel will look at the following question: 

"What should a public library offer everyone in the town, and who should pay for it?"

The Public Panel on Libraries will be held on the following dates:

●    13-15 November 2026 - London 
●    5-6 December 2026 - Birmingham
●    9-10 January 2027 - Birmingham
●    16 March 2027 - online
●    20-21 March 2027 – Birmingham or London (to be confirmed closer to the time)
●    13 April 2027 - online
●    17-18 April 2027 - Birmingham or London (to be confirmed closer to the time)

There will be an introductory dinner on Friday 13 November from 6.30pm. This will be an opportunity to be introduced to the topic and your fellow participants. 

If you are selected and take part in all 12 sessions you will get £1600 in recognition of your time and contribution. If there is anything we can do to help you to take part, we are happy to discuss this with you. Please register to join the Public Panel on Libraries whatever your situation, and someone will be in touch if you are selected to take part.

If you need help registering or have other questions please call our Freephone number 0808 157 0123. Lines are open 8am–8pm every day. You can also email questions to hello@civic-lottery.example.org

IMPORTANT NOTES:

  • Everyone who registers online must have their own email address. If you do not have an email address, please ring the Freephone number above to register.

  • All fields marked with an asterisk (*) must be completed.

  • If selected, Civic Lottery Trust will share all your details with Northgate Insight, the organisation running the Public Panel on Libraries. They will make a separate data agreement with you if you are selected to take part. Your data will be kept strictly confidential. Civic Lottery Trust will delete your details three months after the Public Panel on Libraries ends, unless you tell them otherwise below. Please read both Civic Lottery Trust's Privacy Policy and Northgate Insight's Privacy Notice for more details.

  • Participating in the Public Panel on Libraries is entirely voluntary. You can ask Civic Lottery Trust to delete your data, or request a copy of it, by emailing privacy@civic-lottery.example.org.

  • There may be a film crew who attend some part of the in-person sessions to film and take photos of the process but it is entirely up to participants if they want to be involved in this or not. The footage would be shared with selected media to illustrate how the process works to the general public. No details of participant discussions will be filmed, to preserve anonymity of views. We will make your choices clear on how you can opt in or out of this.
